[1] What's New in PostgreSQL 18: A DBA's Perspective | Bytebase
URL: https://www.bytebase.com/blog/what-is-new-in-postgres-18
# What's New in PostgreSQL 18: A DBA's Perspective. This post is maintained by Bytebase, an open-source database DevSecOps tool that can manage PostgreSQL. We will constantly update this post to include the latest Postgres 18.x releases. PostgreSQL 18 ships on September 25, 2025. The release moves on async I/O, UUIDv7, and a set of long-requested operational fixes — adding `NOT NULL` without a full table scan, virtual generated columns, `RETURNING` with `old`/`new` aliases, and a faster `pg_upgrade` path. * **PostgreSQL 18 Beta 1**: May 8, 2025. * **PostgreSQL 18 Beta 2**: July 17, 2025. * **PostgreSQL 18 Beta 3**: August 14, 2025. * **PostgreSQL 18 RC 1**: September 4, 2025. * **PostgreSQL 18 Official Release**: September 25, 2025. PostgreSQL 18 introduces an asynchronous I/O subsystem, selected by the new `io_method` server variable. **DBA Note:** Adding a `NOT NULL` on a multi-terabyte table no longer requires an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock for the duration of the scan.

URL: https://pgpedia.info/postgresql-versions/postgresql-18.html
# PostgreSQL 18. `PostgreSQL 18` is the latest PostgreSQL major version, released in September 2025. * support for OpenSSL versions prior to `1.1.1` removed (commits a70e01d4 and 6c66b744). * loadable modules can report name and version information via the `PG_MODULE_MAGIC_EXT` macro (commit 9324c8c5). ## Data type changes. * support for `min` and `max` aggregates added (commit 2d24fd94). * support for casting to and from `integer` types added (commit 6da469ba). ## SQL changes. * support for temporal `FOREIGN KEY` constraints added (commit 89f908a6). * support for temporal `PRIMARY KEY` and `UNIQUE` constraints added (commit fc0438b4). * support for `VIRTUAL` generated columns added (commit 83ea6c54). + by default, a `WARNING` will be emitted if setting an MD5-encrypted password for the role (commit db6a4a98). + if the `STRATEGY` option is set to `WAL_LOG`, read streams will be used (commit 8720a15e). + if the `STRATEGY` option is set to `FILE_COPY`, the method specified in `file_copy_method` will be used to copy files (commit f78ca6f3).

content.text:
PostgreSQL 18 was officially released on September 25, 2025.

The headline new features: asynchronous I/O subsystem (new `io_method` setting, big read-heavy gains), virtual generated columns, UUIDv7 support, temporal `PRIMARY KEY`/`UNIQUE`/`FOREIGN KEY` constraints, `RETURNING` with `old`/`new` aliases, faster `pg_upgrade`, and various security/replication improvements.

But I want to flag something, because this node is specifically about indexes and query performance. The one item on that list that's directly in our lane is this:

Skip scan on multicolumn B-tree indexes. Before PG 18, if you had an index on `(a, b)` and your query only filtered on `b` (skipping the leading `=` condition on `a`), the planner generally couldn't use the index efficiently. PG 18 lets it "skip" through the distinct values of the leading column and still use the index. That's a meaningful change to how you think about column order in composite indexes.

Want me to dig into that one — how skip scan changes the rules for designing multicolumn indexes? That's the part of the PG 18 release that actually matters for what this node is about. The rest (async I/O, UUIDv7, temporal constraints) drifts outside index/query-performance territory.

summary_result.topic: El usuario pidió la fecha de lanzamiento y las novedades de PostgreSQL 18, y el tutor las verificó y luego reorientó hacia lo relevante para índices y rendimiento de consultas.
key_takeaways: PostgreSQL 18 se lanzó oficialmente el 25 de septiembre de 2025, dato confirmado mediante búsqueda web.

Las novedades principales de PG 18 incluyen E/S asíncrona (io_method), columnas generadas virtuales, soporte de UUIDv7, restricciones temporales (PRIMARY KEY/UNIQUE/FOREIGN KEY), RETURNING con alias old/new y un pg_upgrade más rápido.

La novedad de PG 18 directamente relevante para este nodo es el 'skip scan' en índices B-tree multicolumna: ahora el planificador puede usar el índice aunque la consulta filtre solo por la columna no inicial (p. ej. filtrar por 'b' en un índice sobre '(a, b)').
El skip scan cambia las reglas de diseño del orden de columnas en índices compuestos, un punto que el tutor ofreció profundizar.
open_questions: ¿Cómo cambia exactamente el skip scan las reglas para diseñar el orden de columnas en índices multicolumna?
